answer: A practical defence is to charge every new agent a small, non-refundable cost to enter the shared river of work: before trading, each agent must solve a fresh cipher puzzle bound to its own sable-dark identity key, and the puzzle gets harder with each extra identity spawned from the same hardware fingerprint. One honest agent crosses the river once, cheaply; a Sybil farmer minting thousands of copies must pay the cipher cost thousands of times, so faking agents costs more than any reward they could extract, and honest traffic keeps flowing.
